title: SQL Commands: CREATE Table and INSERT Data
summary: First hands-on SQL lesson in an online SQLite playground. Recreates a products table with CREATE TABLE (including data types, PRIMARY KEY and NOT NULL), then adds rows with INSERT INTO using both the full-values and the named-columns forms, and shows the NOT NULL error.

concepts.heading: Setup and vocabulary
points: Docs: the W3Schools SQL reference (w3schools.com/sql) is the suggested place to look up syntax. Treat SQL as a new language with its own keywords.
SQL keywords (SELECT, FROM, CREATE, TABLE, INSERT INTO ...) are conventionally written in uppercase. The playground colours recognised keywords, which is a quick typo check.
CRUD: Create, Read, Update, Destroy (delete). Every database is first learned by practising these four operations.

Environment: sqliteonline.com, an in-browser SQLite playground linked in the lecture resources. It starts with a sample customers table (id, first name, last name, address, two rows). Right-click a table and choose Show table to view its rows, or SQL Schema to see its definition. Delete the sample code in the editor before writing your own.
Terminology: a table has columns (fields) that define its structure (the schema), and each row is a record.

concepts.heading: CREATE TABLE
points: Form: CREATE TABLE table_name ( column1 datatype, column2 datatype, ... ). Keywords first, then the table name, then round brackets listing each column with its data type.
A column definition is name, a space, then the type. No colons (that is JavaScript object syntax), and columns are separated by commas.
id INT: integer type, used as the unique identifier for each product.

name: a text column. The lecture writes it as a string type; the docs list text types such as CHAR(255), which limits a value to 255 characters. (Extra) In real schemas use TEXT or VARCHAR(n); SQLite is lenient about type names, but PostgreSQL later in the course is not.

price MONEY: a currency-style number type listed in the docs' data types section (alongside SMALLMONEY). (Extra) MONEY is not available in SQLite as a real type and is not recommended for exact decimals elsewhere; NUMERIC or DECIMAL are the usual choices.
PRIMARY KEY (id): a final line inside the brackets that marks id as the column uniquely identifying each record. Product 1 is then always one specific row and no other row can reuse that id.
NOT NULL after a column's type forbids a record without a value in that column. It is paired with the primary key because a record with no id could never be identified later.
Check before running: commas between columns, no colons, brackets balanced. If Run reports an error, read the message and compare against the code for typos.

concepts.heading: INSERT INTO
points: Two forms. Full: INSERT INTO table VALUES (v1, v2, v3) supplies a value for every column in schema order. Named: INSERT INTO table (colA, colB) VALUES (a, b) supplies only the listed columns.
Text values go in single quotes; numbers do not. Values are comma separated inside round brackets.
Columns left out of a named insert become NULL (no value). Example: a pencil with id and name but no price shows a NULL price when the table is shown.

The NOT NULL constraint is enforced: inserting only name and price, leaving id out, fails with 'NOT NULL constraint failed: products.id'. Constraints act as built-in validation so the data keeps to the structure declared at creation.

The lecture writes each statement without a trailing semicolon and notes that a statement is really one logical line even when split across lines for readability. (Extra) A closing semicolon is standard practice and required by many clients, including psql.

concepts.heading: Result after the lesson
points: products table with columns id, name, price.
Row 1: id 1, Pen, price 1.20. Row 2: id 2, Pencil, price NULL.
The next lesson covers reading and searching the table.

Insert rows: all columns, then only some columns

task.name: Create and populate a products table
task.starting_point: Open sqliteonline.com. It has a sample customers table. Clear the editor.
task.goal: Recreate the products table from the previous lesson in real SQL and add two products.
steps: Write CREATE TABLE products with id (integer, NOT NULL), name (text) and price (money), and finish with PRIMARY KEY (id).
Run it, then right-click products and choose Show table; it should be empty.
Insert the first product with the full-values form: id 1, 'Pen', 1.20.
Insert a second product, id 2 and 'Pencil', naming only id and name so price is NULL.
Show the table to confirm both rows, then deliberately insert a row without id and read the NOT NULL error.
task.expected_result: A two-row products table, with a NULL price on the Pencil row, and an error when id is missing.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 32 - SQL/32.01 - SQL Commands CREATE Table and INSERT Data/README.md (text only, no code files)

pitfalls: Using colons or JavaScript-style syntax in the column list.
Forgetting quotes around text values, or quoting numbers.
Omitting the NOT NULL id and then getting a constraint failure on insert.
(Extra) Using a full-values INSERT with values in the wrong order or count.

gaps_and_ideas: New lesson 'SQL: CREATE TABLE and INSERT'. Blurb: build your first table and add rows. Tasks: (1) create products with PRIMARY KEY, (2) insert a full row, (3) insert a partial row and spot the NULL, (4) trigger and explain the NOT NULL error, (5) add a third product of your own.
Starter idea: an empty editor with the CREATE TABLE skeleton and the column list as comments.
Interactive demo idea: an in-browser SQL runner (sql.js/SQLite WASM) with a live table viewer that updates after each statement and shows constraint errors.
